title.zh: 卷一百〇一 列傳第三十九: 承暉本名福興 抹撚盡忠 僕散端本名七斤 耿端義 李英 孛朮魯德裕 烏古論慶壽
title.en: Volume 101 Biographies 39: Cheng Hui former name Fu Xing, Monian Jinzhong, Pu Sanduan former name Qi Jin, Geng Duanyi, Li Ying, Bei Pailudeyu, Wugulunqingshou
title.raw: 卷一百〇一 列傳第三十九: 承暉本名福興 抹撚盡忠 僕散端本名七斤 耿端義 李英 孛朮魯德裕 烏古論慶壽 Volume 101 Biographies 39: Cheng Hui former name Fu Xing, Monian Jinzhong, Pu Sanduan former name Qi Jin, Geng Duanyi, Li Ying, Bei Pailudeyu, Wugulunqingshou

sentences.zh: 承暉，字維明，本名福興。

translations.literal: Cheng Hui, courtesy name Weiming, original name Fu Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Hui, whose courtesy name was Weiming, had originally been named Fu Xing.

sentences.zh: 好學，淹貫經史。

translations.literal: He loved learning and was thoroughly versed in the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: A devoted scholar, he possessed a thorough command of the classics and historical works.

sentences.zh: 襲父益都尹鄭家塔割剌訛沒謀克。

translations.literal: He inherited his father's post as gelal emo mouke at Zhengjiata under the Yidu prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He succeeded his father as gelal emo mouke at Zhengjiata under the prefect of Yidu.

sentences.zh: 大定十五年，選充符寶祗候，遷筆硯直長，轉近侍局直長，調中都右警巡使。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Dading, he was selected as tally-and-seal attendant, promoted to director of the Brush and Ink Office, transferred to director of the Palace Attendants Bureau, and appointed right patrol commissioner of the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of the Dading reign (1175), he was chosen as a tally-and-seal attendant, rose to head the Brush and Ink Office, became director of the Palace Attendants Bureau, and was transferred to serve as right patrol commissioner of the Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 章宗為皇太孫，選充侍正。

translations.literal: When Zhangzong was heir apparent, Cheng was selected as director of attendance.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhangzong was still heir apparent, Cheng was appointed director of attendance in his household.

sentences.zh: 章宗即位，遷近侍局使。

translations.literal: When Zhangzong ascended the throne, Cheng was promoted to commissioner of the Palace Attendants Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhangzong took the throne, Cheng was made commissioner of the Palace Attendants Bureau.

sentences.zh: 孝懿皇后妹夫吾也藍，世宗時以罪斥去，乙夜，詔開宮城門召之。

translations.literal: Wuyelan, brother-in-law of Empress Xiaoyi, had been dismissed for a crime in Shizong's time; at the second watch of the night an edict ordered the palace gates opened to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyelan, a brother-in-law of Empress Xiaoyi, had been banished for an offense during Shizong's reign; late one night the emperor ordered the palace gates opened to summon him back.

sentences.zh: 承暉不奉詔，明日奏曰：「吾也藍得罪先帝，不可召。

translations.literal: Cheng Hui did not carry out the edict; the next day he memorialized, saying, "Wuyelan offended the late emperor and must not be summoned."
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Hui refused to obey the order; the next morning he memorialized, "Wuyelan offended the late emperor and must not be recalled."

sentences.zh: 」章宗曰：「善。

translations.literal: " Zhangzong said, "Good."
translations.idiomatic: " Zhangzong replied, "Well said."

sentences.zh: 」未幾，遷兵部侍郎兼右補闕。

translations.literal: " Before long he was promoted to vice minister of War and concurrently right remonstrance official.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon afterward he was promoted to vice minister of War while also serving as right remonstrance official.

sentences.zh: 初置九路提刑司，承暉東京咸平等路提刑副使，改同知上京留守事。

translations.literal: When the nine-route judicial commissioners were first established, Cheng Hui became deputy judicial commissioner for the Eastern Capital and Xianping circuits, then was transferred to deputy commissioner of the Shangjing garrison command.
translations.idiomatic: When the nine-route judicial commissioner offices were first set up, Cheng served as deputy commissioner on the Eastern Capital and Xianping circuits, and later became deputy commissioner of the Shangjing garrison command.

sentences.zh: 御史台奏：「承暉前為提刑，豪猾屏息。

translations.literal: The Censorate memorialized, "When Cheng Hui previously served as judicial commissioner, the powerful and unscrupulous fell silent."
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate reported, "In Cheng Hui's earlier term as judicial commissioner, local bullies were cowed into silence."

sentences.zh: 」遷臨海軍節度使。

translations.literal: " He was transferred to military commissioner of the Linhai Army.
translations.idiomatic: " He was then appointed military commissioner of the Linhai Army.

sentences.zh: 曆利涉、遼海軍，遷北京路提刑使。

translations.literal: He served in succession at Lisher and Liaohai armies, then was promoted to judicial commissioner of the Northern Capital circuit.
translations.idiomatic: After successive postings with the Lisher and Liaohai armies, he was made judicial commissioner of the Northern Capital circuit.

sentences.zh: 曆知咸平、臨潢府，為北京留守。

translations.literal: He served in succession as prefect of Xianping and Linhuang, then became garrison commissioner of the Northern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He later governed Xianping and Linhuang in turn before becoming garrison commissioner of the Northern Capital.

sentences.zh: 副留守李東陽素貴，承暉自非公事，不與交一言。

translations.literal: The deputy garrison commissioner Li Dongyang was by nature arrogant; except on public business Cheng Hui would not exchange a single word with him.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy garrison commissioner Li Dongyang was notoriously haughty; Cheng would not speak to him at all except on official business.

sentences.zh: 改知大名府，召為刑部尚書，兼知審官院。

translations.literal: He was transferred to administer Daming Prefecture, then summoned as minister of Justice and concurrently director of the Bureau for Review of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to govern Daming Prefecture, he was soon recalled to serve as minister of Justice while also overseeing the Bureau for Review of Appointments.

sentences.zh: 惠民司都監餘裏痕都遷織染署直長，承暉駁奏曰：「痕都以廕得官，別無才能，前為大陽渡譏察，才八月擢惠民司都監，已為太優，依格兩除之後，當再入監差，今乃超授隨朝八品職任。

translations.literal: Yulihandu, chief superintendent of the Bureau of Public Benefit, was transferred to director of the Dyeing Office; Cheng Hui rebutted in a memorial, saying, "Handu gained office by hereditary privilege and has no other ability. Formerly inspector at Dayang Ford, after only eight months he was promoted to chief superintendent of the Bureau of Public Benefit, which was already too generous. By regulation, after two appointments he should return to a supervisory post, yet now he is leapfrogged into an eighth-rank court office."
translations.idiomatic: When Yulihandu, chief superintendent of the Bureau of Public Benefit, was slated for promotion to director of the Dyeing Office, Cheng Hui objected in a memorial: "Handu owes his post to hereditary privilege and has shown no talent elsewhere. As inspector at Dayang Ford for only eight months he was already raised to head the Bureau of Public Benefit—an excessive favor. Regulations require that after two terms he return to a supervisory assignment; instead he is being jumped ahead into an eighth-rank post at court."

sentences.zh: 況痕都乃平章鎰之甥，不能不涉物議。

translations.literal: Moreover Handu is a nephew of Grand Councilor Yi; this cannot but invite public criticism."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Handu is a nephew of Grand Councilor Yi—appointment like this is bound to draw public censure."

sentences.zh: 」上從承暉議，召徒單鎰深責之。

translations.literal: " The emperor followed Cheng Hui's view, summoned Tushan Yi, and rebuked him severely.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor accepted Cheng Hui's argument, summoned Tushan Yi, and reprimanded him sharply.

sentences.zh: 改知大興府事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to administer the Daxing metropolitan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned to govern the metropolitan prefecture of Daxing.

sentences.zh: 宦者李新喜有寵用事，借大興府妓樂。

translations.literal: The eunuch Li Xinxhi, favored and wielding power, borrowed the prefecture's courtesans and musicians.
translations.idiomatic: The favored eunuch Li Xinxhi, who held real influence at court, demanded the use of Daxing's courtesans and musicians.

sentences.zh: 承暉拒不與，新喜慚。

translations.literal: Cheng Hui refused to grant them; Xinxhi was ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Hui refused, leaving Xinxhi humiliated.

sentences.zh: 章宗聞而嘉之。

translations.literal: Zhangzong heard of it and praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhangzong heard of this, he commended Cheng Hui.

sentences.zh: 豪民與人爭種稻水利不直，厚賂元妃兄左宣徽使李仁惠。

translations.literal: A powerful local man disputing rice-planting water rights was in the wrong and lavished bribes on Li Renhui, the primary consort's brother and left commissioner of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: A wealthy bully who was clearly in the wrong in a dispute over irrigation for rice paddies paid a heavy bribe to Li Renhui, brother of the primary consort and left commissioner of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 仁惠使人屬承暉右之。

translations.literal: Renhui sent someone to ask Cheng Hui to decide in his favor.
translations.idiomatic: Renhui sent an intermediary urging Cheng to rule in the bully's favor.

sentences.zh: 承暉即杖豪民而遣之，謂其人曰：「可以此報宣徽也。

translations.literal: Cheng Hui immediately had the powerful man beaten with the staff and sent away, telling the messenger, "You may report this to the Secretariat commissioner."
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Hui had the bully flogged at once and dismissed him, telling the envoy, "Take that back to the Secretariat commissioner as my answer."

sentences.zh: 」複改知大名府事。

translations.literal: " He was again transferred to administer Daming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: " He was transferred once more to govern Daming Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 雨潦害稼，承暉決引潦水納之濠隍。

translations.literal: Rain floods damaged the crops; Cheng Hui opened channels to divert the floodwater into the moat.
translations.idiomatic: When heavy rains ruined the harvest, Cheng Hui cut channels to drain the flood into the city moat.

sentences.zh: 及伐宋，遷山東路統軍使。

translations.literal: When the campaign against Song began, he was transferred to commander-in-chief of the Shandong circuit.
translations.idiomatic: At the outbreak of war with Song, he was appointed commander-in-chief of the Shandong circuit.

sentences.zh: 山東盜賊起，承暉言：「捕盜不即獲，比奏報或遷官去官，請權行的決。

translations.literal: Bandits rose in Shandong; Cheng Hui said, "When bandits are not captured at once, by the time a report is filed the official may have been transferred or dismissed; I request provisional authority to decide on the spot."
translations.idiomatic: As banditry spread in Shandong, Cheng Hui argued, "If arrests are delayed until memorials reach the capital, the responsible officer may already have been transferred or removed; grant temporary authority to decide cases on the spot."

sentences.zh: 」尚書省議：「猛安依舊收贖，謀克奏報，其餘鈐轄都軍巡尉先決奏聞，俟事定復舊。

translations.literal: " The Ministry deliberated: "Meng'an offices shall continue to accept ransoms; mouke offices shall report upward; other garrison commanders, army inspectors, and patrol officers may decide first and then report, reverting to former practice once the situation stabilizes."
translations.idiomatic: " The Ministry of Civil Appointments ruled that meng'an units could still accept ransoms, mouke units must report upward, and other garrison commanders, army inspectors, and patrol officers might judge cases locally and report afterward, returning to normal procedure once order was restored."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The proposal was adopted.

sentences.zh: 及罷兵，盜賊渠魁稍就招降，猶往往潛匿泰山岩穴間。

translations.literal: When the army stood down, the bandit chiefs gradually accepted surrender, yet many still hid in the caves of Mount Tai.
translations.idiomatic: After the troops were withdrawn, many bandit leaders accepted amnesty, but others continued to hide in the caves of Mount Tai.

sentences.zh: 按察司請發數萬人刊除林木，則盜賊無所隱矣。

translations.literal: The surveillance commission requested tens of thousands of men to clear-cut the forest so the bandits would have nowhere to hide.
translations.idiomatic: The surveillance commission proposed sending tens of thousands of laborers to strip the mountain of trees so the bandits could no longer find cover.

sentences.zh: 承暉奏曰：「泰山五嶽之宗，故曰岱宗。

translations.literal: Cheng Hui memorialized, saying, "Mount Tai is the head of the Five Sacred Peaks, hence called the Peak of the East."
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Hui objected in a memorial: "Mount Tai stands at the head of the Five Sacred Peaks and is therefore called the Eastern Peak."

sentences.zh: 王者受命，封禪告代，國家雖不行此事，而山亦不可赭也。

translations.literal: When a king receives the Mandate he performs the feng and shan rites to announce the change of dynasty; though our state does not carry out this ceremony, the mountain still must not be laid bare.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler receives Heaven's mandate he ascends it to perform the feng and shan rites; even though our dynasty does not hold those ceremonies, the mountain must not be stripped bare.

sentences.zh: 齊人易動，驅之入山，必有凍餓失所之患，此誨盜，非止盜也。

translations.literal: The people of Qi are easily stirred; driving them into the mountains will surely bring suffering from cold, hunger, and homelessness—this teaches banditry, not merely fails to stop it.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Qi are quick to rise in unrest; herding them into the hills will only multiply deaths from cold and hunger and create refugees—such a policy would teach men to become bandits, not merely fail to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 天下之山亦多矣，豈可盡赭哉。

translations.literal: There are many mountains under Heaven—can they all be laid bare?"
translations.idiomatic: There are countless mountains in the realm—are we to lay bare every one of them?"

sentences.zh: 」議遂寢。

translations.literal: " The proposal was then dropped.
translations.idiomatic: " The plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 中都被圍，承暉出議和事。

translations.literal: When the Central Capital was besieged, Cheng Hui went out to negotiate peace.
translations.idiomatic: When the Central Capital came under siege, Cheng Hui was sent out to negotiate peace.

sentences.zh: 宣宗遷汴，進拜右丞相，兼都元帥，徙封定國公，與皇太子留守中都。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong moved the court to Bian, Cheng was promoted to right grand councilor and concurrently supreme commander, enfeoffed as Duke of Dingguo, and left with the heir apparent to hold the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: After Xuanzong relocated to Bian, Cheng was made right grand councilor and supreme commander, enfeoffed as Duke of Dingguo, and charged with holding the Central Capital alongside the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 承暉以尚書左丞抹撚盡忠久在軍旅，知兵事，遂以赤心委盡忠，悉以兵事付之，己乃總持大綱，期於保完都城。

translations.literal: Cheng Hui, seeing that Left Vice Minister Monian Jinzhong had long served in the army and understood military affairs, entrusted him with his whole heart, handing over all military matters, while he himself held the overall plan, hoping to preserve the capital intact.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing that Left Vice Minister Monian Jinzhong had long campaigned in the field and understood warfare, Cheng entrusted him wholeheartedly with all military affairs while he himself held overall direction, determined to preserve the capital.

sentences.zh: 頃之，莊獻太子去之，右副元帥蒲察七斤以其軍出降，中都危急。

translations.literal: Before long the heir apparent Zhuangxian departed; the right deputy commander Pucha Qijin surrendered with his army; the Central Capital was in dire peril.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the heir apparent Zhuangxian left the city; right deputy commander Pucha Qijin surrendered with his troops; and the Central Capital faced imminent collapse.

sentences.zh: 詔以抹撚盡忠為平章政事，兼左副元帥。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Monian Jinzhong grand councilor and concurrently left deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Monian Jinzhong grand councilor and left deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 三年二月，詔元帥左監軍永錫將中山、真定兵，元帥左都監烏古論慶壽將大名軍萬八千人、西南路步騎萬一千、河北兵一萬，御史中丞李英運糧，參知政事、大名行省孛朮魯德裕調遣繼發，救中都。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year an edict ordered Left Army Supervisor Yongxi to lead the Zhongshan and Zhending forces, Left Army Director Wugulun Qingshou to lead eighteen thousand from the Daming army, eleven thousand infantry and cavalry of the Southwest circuit, and ten thousand Hebei troops; Censor-in-chief Li Ying to transport grain; and Vice Grand Councilor and Daming branch secretariat Bei Pailu Deyu to organize successive dispatches to relieve the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the third year (1215) the court ordered Left Army Supervisor Yongxi to march the Zhongshan and Zhending armies, Left Army Director Wugulun Qingshou to lead eighteen thousand Daming troops plus eleven thousand Southwest circuit horse and foot and ten thousand Hebei soldiers, Censor-in-chief Li Ying to convoy supplies, and Vice Grand Councilor Bei Pailu Deyu of the Daming branch secretariat to coordinate follow-on columns—all to rescue the Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 承暉間遣人以礬寫奏曰：「七斤既降，城中無有固志，臣雖以死守之，豈能持久。

translations.literal: Cheng Hui sent men at intervals to write memorials in alum fluid, saying, "Now that Qijin has surrendered, the city has no firm will to resist; though I die defending it, how can that last long?"
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Hui repeatedly sent couriers bearing memorials written in alum ink: "With Qijin already surrendered, the city has lost the will to hold out; though I am ready to die in its defense, how long can that endure?"

sentences.zh: 伏念一失中都，遼東、河朔皆非我有，諸軍倍道來援，猶冀有濟。

translations.literal: I reflect that once the Central Capital is lost, Liaodong and the north of the Yellow River will no longer be ours; if the armies hurry by forced marches to aid us, there may still be hope."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to consider that if the Central Capital falls, Liaodong and Hebei will slip from our grasp; if the relief columns march at utmost speed, success may yet be possible."

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「中都重地，廟社在焉，朕豈一日忘也。

translations.literal: " An edict replied, "The Central Capital is a vital place; the altars of state stand there—how could I forget it for a single day?"
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor answered, "The Central Capital is the heart of the realm; our ancestral altars stand there—how could I forget it even for a day?"

sentences.zh: 已趣諸路兵與糧俱往，卿會知之。

translations.literal: Troops and grain from all circuits have already been hastened thither—you will understand."
translations.idiomatic: Troops and grain from every circuit are already on the march—you will soon know it."

sentences.zh: 」及詔中都官吏軍民曰：「朕欲紓民力，遂幸陪都，天未悔禍，時尚多虞，道路久梗，音問難通。

translations.literal: " There was also an edict to the officials, soldiers, and people of the Central Capital, saying, "I wished to ease the people's burdens and therefore visited the secondary capital; Heaven has not yet turned from calamity, and the times are still full of peril; the roads have long been blocked and messages hard to pass."
translations.idiomatic: " The court also issued an edict to the officials, troops, and populace of the Central Capital: "I moved to the secondary capital to spare your burdens; Heaven has not yet lifted its scourge, dangers remain on every side, the roads have been cut for months, and word from the court has scarcely reached you."

sentences.zh: 汝等朝暮矢石，暴露風霜，思惟報國，靡有貳心，俟兵事之稍息，當不愆地旌賞。

translations.literal: You face arrows and stones morning and evening, endure wind and frost in the open, think only of repaying the state, and have no second heart; when military affairs ease a little, rewards will not fall short of what is due."
translations.idiomatic: Day and night you endure arrows and stones and hardship in the open, loyal in thought and deed; when the fighting subsides, your rewards will not be stinted."

sentences.zh: 今已會合諸路兵馬救援，故茲獎諭，想宜知悉。

translations.literal: Now troops from all circuits have been assembled for relief; therefore this commendation is issued—may you all understand."
translations.idiomatic: Relief forces from every circuit are now converging; take this message as encouragement and assurance."

sentences.zh: 」永錫、慶壽等軍至霸州北。

translations.literal: " The armies of Yongxi, Qingshou, and others reached north of Bazhou.
translations.idiomatic: " Yongxi, Qingshou, and the other columns reached the country north of Bazhou.

sentences.zh: 三月乙亥，李英被酒，軍無紀律，大元兵攻之，英軍大敗。

translations.literal: On yihai of the third month Li Ying was drunk; the army lacked discipline; the Great Yuan forces attacked and Ying's army was utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: On the yihai day of the third month Li Ying was intoxicated, his troops were undisciplined, the Yuan army struck, and his force was routed.

sentences.zh: 是時，高琪居中用事，忌承暉成功，諸將皆顧望。

translations.literal: At this time Gao Qi held power at court, envied Cheng Hui's success, and the generals all hesitated and looked about.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Qi then dominated the court, resented any success that might bolster Cheng Hui, and the generals hung back in indecision.

sentences.zh: 既而以刑部侍郎阿典宋阿為左監軍，行元帥府于清州，同知真定府事女奚烈胡論出為右都監，行元帥府于保州，戶部侍郎侯摯行尚書六部，往來應給，終無一兵至中都者。

translations.literal: Then Vice Minister of Justice Adian Song'a was made left army supervisor with the marshal's staff at Qingzhou; Deputy Prefect of Zhending Nüxilie Hulu was made right army director with the marshal's staff at Baozhou; Vice Minister of Revenue Hou Zhi directed the Six Ministries of the Secretariat, shuttling back and forth to supply needs—yet in the end not a single soldier reached the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Song'a of the Adian clan was then named left army supervisor with headquarters at Qingzhou; Nüxilie Hulu, deputy prefect of Zhending, became right army director at Baozhou; Hou Zhi of the Revenue Ministry ran the six secretariat departments, shuttling supplies—yet not one soldier ever reached the Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 慶壽軍聞之亦潰。

translations.literal: Qingshou's army, hearing of this, also collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: On hearing the news, Qingshou's army disintegrated as well.

sentences.zh: 承暉與抹撚盡忠會議於尚書省。

translations.literal: Cheng Hui and Monian Jinzhong met in council at the Ministry of Civil Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Hui and Monian Jinzhong conferred at the Ministry of Civil Appointments.

sentences.zh: 承暉約盡忠同死社稷。

translations.literal: Cheng Hui pledged that Jinzhong would die with him for the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Hui bound Jinzhong to die with him defending the altars of state.

sentences.zh: 盡忠謀南奔，承暉怒，即起還第，亦無如盡忠何。

translations.literal: Jinzhong plotted to flee south; Cheng Hui was angry, rose at once and returned to his residence, yet could do nothing about Jinzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhong planned to flee south; enraged, Cheng Hui rose and left for his mansion, powerless to stop him.

sentences.zh: 召盡忠腹心元帥府經歷官完顏師姑至，謂曰：「始我謂平章知兵，故推心以權畀平章，嘗許與我俱死。

translations.literal: He summoned Jinzhong's confidant, the marshal's staff administrator Wanyan Shigu, and said, "At first I thought the grand councilor understood warfare, so I entrusted him with my whole heart and delegated authority to him, and he once promised to die with me."
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Jinzhong's trusted marshal's staff officer Wanyan Shigu and said, "I once believed the grand councilor knew war, opened my heart to him, and gave him full command; he even pledged to die with me."

sentences.zh: 今忽異議，行期且在何日，汝必知之。

translations.literal: Now he suddenly changes his mind—on what day is the departure set? You must know."
translations.idiomatic: Now he breaks his word—when does he plan to leave? You must know."

sentences.zh: 」師姑曰：「今日向暮且行。

translations.literal: " Shigu said, "This very evening, toward dusk, he will go."
translations.idiomatic: " Shigu replied, "He means to leave this evening at dusk."

sentences.zh: 」曰：「汝行李辦未？

translations.literal: " Cheng said, "Are your traveling goods ready?"
translations.idiomatic: " Cheng asked, "Have you packed your baggage?"

translations.literal: " He said, "They are ready."
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "They are ready."

sentences.zh: 承暉變色曰：「社稷若何？

translations.literal: Cheng Hui's countenance changed as he said, "What of the altars of state?"
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Hui's face darkened. "What of the altars of state?" he demanded.

sentences.zh: 」師姑不能對。

translations.literal: " Shigu could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: " Shigu had no reply.

sentences.zh: 叱下斬之。

translations.literal: He ordered him taken down and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: He had Shigu dragged away and executed.

sentences.zh: 承暉起，辭謁家廟，召左右司郎中趙思文與之飲酒，謂之曰：「事勢至此，惟有一死以報國家。

translations.literal: Cheng Hui rose, took leave at the family shrine, summoned Zhao Siwen of the Left and Right Secretariat to drink with him, and said, "Matters have come to this pass; there is only death by which to repay the state."
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Hui rose, paid his respects at the family shrine, called in Zhao Siwen of the Left and Right Secretariat for a final drink, and told him, "Matters stand here; only death remains with which to repay the state."

sentences.zh: 」作遺表付尚書省令史師安石。

translations.literal: " He composed a final memorial and entrusted it to the secretariat clerk Shi Anshi.
translations.idiomatic: " He drafted a death memorial and gave it to the secretariat clerk Shi Anshi.

sentences.zh: 其表皆論國家大計，辨君子小人治亂之本，曆指當時邪正者數人，曰：「平章政事高琪，賦性陰險，報復私憾，竊弄威柄，包藏禍心，終害國家。

translations.literal: The memorial discussed the great plans of state, distinguished the roots of order and disorder in the conduct of gentlemen and petty men, and named several of the wicked and upright of the time, saying, "Grand Councilor Gao Qi is by nature sinister, repays private grudges, usurps authority, harbors evil intent, and will in the end harm the state."
translations.idiomatic: The memorial addressed the great affairs of state, traced how gentlemen and petty men make or unmake order, and named several contemporaries, declaring, "Grand Councilor Gao Qi is treacherous by nature, nurses private vendettas, abuses power, conceals malice, and will ultimately ruin the dynasty."

sentences.zh: 」因引咎以不能終保都城為謝。

translations.literal: " He took blame upon himself for failing to preserve the capital to the end.
translations.idiomatic: " He accepted blame for his failure to hold the capital to the end.

sentences.zh: 複謂妻子死于滄州，為書以從兄子永懷為後。

translations.literal: He also said his wife and children had died at Cangzhou and wrote a document making his cousin's son Yonghuai his heir.
translations.idiomatic: He noted that his wife and children had perished at Cangzhou and drew up a document naming his cousin's son Yonghuai as his heir.

sentences.zh: 從容若平日，盡出財物，召家人，隨年勞多寡而分之，皆與從良書。

translations.literal: Composed as on an ordinary day, he distributed all his property, summoned the household, divided it according to years of service, and gave each a certificate of manumission.
translations.idiomatic: Calm as on any other day, he gave away his entire estate, gathered his household, divided it according to length of service, and issued each servant a deed of manumission.

sentences.zh: 舉家號泣，承暉神色泰然，方與安石舉白引滿，謂之曰：「承暉於《五經》皆經師授，謹守而力行之，不為虛文。

translations.literal: The whole household wept aloud; Cheng Hui's bearing was serene; just then he raised a cup with Anshi and drained it, saying, "In the Five Classics I was instructed by teachers; I have kept and practiced them diligently, not as empty words."
translations.idiomatic: The household wailed, but Cheng Hui remained composed; he raised his cup with Anshi and drained it, saying, "Every one of the Five Classics I learned from a master; I have kept and lived them, not merely mouthed them."

sentences.zh: 」既被酒，取筆與安石訣，最後倒寫二字，投筆歎曰：「遽爾謬誤，得非神志亂邪？

translations.literal: " Once drunk, he took up the brush to write a farewell to Anshi; at the end he wrote two characters backward, cast down the brush and sighed, "So sudden an error—can my mind not be disturbed?"
translations.idiomatic: " When he was drunk he wrote a parting note to Anshi; at the close he reversed two characters, dropped the brush, and sighed, "Such a slip at once—has my mind already failed?"

sentences.zh: 」謂安石曰：「子行矣。

translations.literal: " He told Anshi, "You may go."
translations.idiomatic: " He told Anshi, "Go now."

sentences.zh: 」安石出門，聞哭聲，複還問之，則已仰藥薨矣。

translations.literal: " Anshi went out; hearing weeping, he returned to ask, and Cheng had already taken poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: " Anshi stepped outside, heard cries of grief, hurried back—and found Cheng Hui already dead from poison he had taken.

sentences.zh: 家人匆匆瘞庭中。

translations.literal: The household hastily buried him in the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: The family buried him hastily in the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 是日暮，盡忠出奔，中都不守。

translations.literal: That evening Jinzhong fled; the Central Capital could no longer be held.
translations.idiomatic: That same evening Jinzhong fled, and the Central Capital fell.

sentences.zh: 貞祐三年五月二日也。

translations.literal: It was the second day of the fifth month in the third year of Zhenyou.
translations.idiomatic: This took place on the second day of the fifth month in the third year of Zhenyou (1215).

sentences.zh: 師安石奉遺表奔赴行在奏之。

translations.literal: Shi Anshi bore the final memorial to the mobile court and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Anshi carried the death memorial to the mobile court and presented it to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 宣宗設奠于相國寺，哭之盡哀。

translations.literal: Xuanzong set out offerings at Xiangguo Temple and wept with the utmost grief.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong offered sacrifices at Xiangguo Temple and mourned him with deepest grief.

sentences.zh: 贈開府儀同三司、太尉、尚書令、廣平郡王，諡忠肅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor with the Three Excellencies of the Palace, Grand Marshal, Director of the Secretariat, and enfeoffed as Prince of Guangping, with the posthumous title Zhongsu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor of the Palace with Three Excellencies, Grand Marshal, Director of the Secretariat, and Prince of Guangping, with the posthumous name Zhongsu (Loyal and Solemn).

sentences.zh: 詔以永懷為器物局直長。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Yonghuai director of the Implements Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Yonghuai director of the Implements Bureau.

sentences.zh: 永懷子撒速為奉禦。

translations.literal: Yonghuai's son Sasu became an imperial attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Yonghuai's son Sasu was appointed an imperial attendant.

sentences.zh: 承暉生而貴富，居家類寒素，常置司馬光、蘇軾像於書室，曰：「吾師司馬而友蘇公。

translations.literal: Cheng Hui was born to wealth and rank, yet at home lived like a poor scholar; he always placed portraits of Sima Guang and Su Shi in his study, saying, "Sima is my teacher and Su my friend."
translations.idiomatic: Though born to wealth and high station, Cheng Hui lived at home like a poor scholar; he kept portraits of Sima Guang and Su Shi in his study, saying, "Sima Guang is my teacher and Su Shi my friend."

sentences.zh: 」平章政事完顏守貞素敬之，與為忘年交。

translations.literal: " Grand Councilor Wanyan Shouzhen had long respected him and became his friend across the difference in age.
translations.idiomatic: " Grand Councilor Wanyan Shouzhen had long admired him and became his close friend despite their difference in years.

sentences.zh: 抹撚盡忠

translations.literal: Monian Jinzhong
translations.idiomatic: Monian Jinzhong

sentences.zh: 抹撚盡忠，本名彖多，上京路猛安人。

translations.literal: Monian Jinzhong, original name Suoduo, was a meng'an man of the Shangjing circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Monian Jinzhong, whose original name was Suoduo, came from a meng'an household of the Shangjing circuit.

sentences.zh: 中大定二十八年進士第，調高陽、朝城主簿，北京、臨潢提刑司知事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year of Dading he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed registrar of Gaoyang and Chaocheng, and served as clerk of the judicial commission of the Northern Capital and Linhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-eighth year of Dading (1188), served as registrar of Gaoyang and Chaocheng, and worked as clerk in the judicial commissions of the Northern Capital and Linhuang.

sentences.zh: 御史台舉廉能，遷順義軍節度副使。

translations.literal: The Censorate recommended him for integrity and ability; he was promoted to deputy military commissioner of the Shunyi Army.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended by the Censorate for integrity and competence, he was made deputy military commissioner of the Shunyi Army.

sentences.zh: 以憂去官，起複翰林修撰，同知德昌軍節度事，簽北京按察司、滑州刺史，改恩州。

translations.literal: He left office in mourning, then was recalled as Hanlin compiler, deputy commissioner of the Dechang army, signatory of the Northern Capital surveillance commission and prefect of Huazhou, then transferred to Enzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After resigning for mourning he was recalled as a Hanlin compiler, made deputy commissioner of the Dechang army, attached to the Northern Capital surveillance commission and appointed prefect of Huazhou, then transferred to Enzhou.

sentences.zh: 上言：「凡買賣軍器，乞令告給憑驗，以防盜賊私市。

translations.literal: He memorialized, saying, "For all trade in military weapons, I request that permits be issued on report, to prevent bandits from buying privately."
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "All sales of military weapons should require registered permits on application, to keep bandits from buying arms in secret."

sentences.zh: 」尚書省議，「止聽系籍人匠貨賣，有知情售不應存留者同私造法。

translations.literal: " The Ministry deliberated that only registered artisans in the rolls might sell, and anyone who knowingly sold items that should not be kept would be punished under the law on private manufacture.
translations.idiomatic: " The Ministry ruled that only registered artisans on the rolls could sell arms, and anyone who knowingly sold prohibited weapons would be punished like a private armorer.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The proposal was adopted.

sentences.zh: 遷山東按察副使，坐虛奏田稼豐收請糴常平粟，詐稱宣差和糴，降虢州刺史，改乾州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to deputy surveillance commissioner of Shandong, then demoted for falsely reporting a bountiful harvest and requesting purchase of Ever-Normal granary grain while fraudulently claiming an imperial commission for equitable purchase; he was reduced to prefect of Guozhou and transferred to Qianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to deputy surveillance commissioner of Shandong, he was later demoted for falsely reporting abundant harvests to obtain Ever-Normal granary grain while posing as an imperial purchasing commissioner; he was reduced to prefect of Guozhou, then moved to Qianzhou.

sentences.zh: 泰和六年，伐宋，為元帥右監軍完顏充經歷官，坐奏報稽滯，杖五十。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taihe, during the campaign against Song, he served as staff officer to Right Army Supervisor Wanyan Chong; for delayed memorials he received fifty strokes of the staff.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Taihe (1206), on the campaign against Song, he served on the staff of Right Army Supervisor Wanyan Chong and was beaten fifty strokes for tardy reports.

sentences.zh: 八年，入為吏部郎中，累遷中都、西京按察使。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he entered the capital as director of the Personnel Bureau, and in succession was promoted to surveillance commissioner of the Central and Western capitals.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he returned to the capital as director of the Personnel Bureau and rose in turn to surveillance commissioner of the Central and Western capitals.

sentences.zh: 是時，紇石烈執中為西京留守，與盡忠爭，私意不協。

translations.literal: At this time Heshilie Zhizhong was garrison commissioner of the Western Capital; he and Jinzhong quarreled and were privately at odds.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Heshilie Zhizhong held the Western Capital as garrison commissioner; he and Jinzhong clashed and bore a private grudge.

sentences.zh: 盡忠陰伺執中過失，申奏。

translations.literal: Jinzhong secretly watched for Zhizhong's faults and reported them.
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhong secretly watched for Zhizhong's missteps and memorialized against him.

sentences.zh: 執中雖跋扈，善撫禦其部曲，密于居庸、北口置腹心刺取按察司文字。

translations.literal: Though Zhizhong was overbearing, he was skilled at controlling his troops; he secretly placed confidants at Juyong and Beikou to intercept surveillance commission documents.
translations.idiomatic: Overbearing though he was, Zhizhong ruled his troops well; he secretly posted agents at Juyong and Beikou to intercept documents from the surveillance commission.

sentences.zh: 及執中自紫荊關走還中都，詔盡忠為左副元帥兼西京留守。

translations.literal: When Zhizhong fled back to the Central Capital from Zijing Pass, an edict appointed Jinzhong left deputy commander and concurrently garrison commissioner of the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhizhong fled from Zijing Pass back to the Central Capital, Jinzhong was named left deputy commander and garrison commissioner of the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 以保全西京功進官三階，賜金百兩、銀千兩、重彩百段、絹二百疋。

translations.literal: For preserving the Western Capital he was promoted three ranks and granted a hundred taels of gold, a thousand taels of silver, a hundred lengths of heavy brocade, and two hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: For saving the Western Capital he was promoted three ranks and rewarded with a hundred taels of gold, a thousand taels of silver, a hundred lengths of heavy brocade, and two hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜尚書右丞，行省西京。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed right vice minister of the Secretariat and branch secretariat of the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he became right vice minister of the Secretariat with charge of the Western Capital branch secretariat.

sentences.zh: 貞祐初，進拜左丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyou he was promoted to left vice minister.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenyou era he was promoted to left vice minister.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「卿總領行省，鎮撫陪京，守禦有功，人民攸賴。

translations.literal: An edict said, "You oversee the branch secretariat, pacify the secondary capital, have merit in defense, and the people rely upon you."
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared, "You direct the branch secretariat, pacify the secondary capital, have distinguished yourself in defense, and the people depend on you."

sentences.zh: 朕新嗣祚，念爾重臣，益勉乃力，以副朕懷。

translations.literal: I have newly succeeded to the throne and think of you as a great minister; strive all the more in your efforts to fulfill my hopes."
translations.idiomatic: I have only lately ascended the throne and count on you as a pillar of the state; redouble your efforts to meet my expectations."

sentences.zh: 」二年五月，自西京入朝，加崇進，封申國公，賜玉帶、金鼎、重幣。

translations.literal: " In the fifth month of the second year he came to court from the Western Capital, was given the honorary title Chongjin, enfeoffed as Duke of Shenguo, and granted a jade belt, a gold tripod, and heavy gifts.
translations.idiomatic: " In the fifth month of the second year he arrived at court from the Western Capital, received the honorary rank Chongjin, was enfeoffed as Duke of Shenguo, and was given a jade belt, a gold tripod, and rich gifts.

sentences.zh: 二年，進拜都元帥，左丞如故。

translations.literal: In the second year he was promoted to supreme commander while retaining the left vice ministership.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was made supreme commander while continuing as left vice minister.

sentences.zh: 宣宗遷汴，與右丞相承暉守中都。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong moved to Bian, Jinzhong and the right grand councilor Cheng Hui held the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong relocated to Bian, Jinzhong joined right grand councilor Cheng Hui in defending the Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 承暉為都元帥，盡忠複為左副元帥。

translations.literal: Cheng Hui was supreme commander; Jinzhong again became left deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Hui served as supreme commander while Jinzhong again became left deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 十月，進拜平章政事，監修國史，左副元帥如故。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he was promoted to grand councilor, supervised compilation of the national history, and retained the left deputy commandership.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he was made grand councilor, placed in charge of compiling the national history, and kept his post as left deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 宣宗詔盡忠善撫颭軍，盡忠不察，殺颭軍數人。

translations.literal: Xuanzong ordered Jinzhong to treat the Fengjun troops well; Jinzhong paid no heed and killed several Fengjun men.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong instructed Jinzhong to treat the Fengjun mercenaries kindly; heedless, Jinzhong had several of them killed.

sentences.zh: 已而中都受圍，承暉以盡忠久在軍旅，付以兵事，嘗約同死社稷。

translations.literal: Before long the Central Capital was besieged; Cheng Hui, seeing that Jinzhong had long been in the army, entrusted him with military affairs and once pledged to die together for the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: When the Central Capital was besieged, Cheng Hui, knowing Jinzhong's long military experience, gave him command of the armies and had once bound him to die together defending the realm.

sentences.zh: 及烏古論慶壽等兵潰，外援不至，中都危急，密與腹心元帥府經歷官完顏師姑謀棄中都南奔，已戒行李，期以五月二日向暮出城。

translations.literal: When the armies of Wugulun Qingshou and others collapsed and outside aid did not arrive, the Central Capital was in peril; Jinzhong secretly plotted with his confidant, marshal's staff administrator Wanyan Shigu, to abandon the capital and flee south, had already ordered baggage prepared, and set the second day of the fifth month at dusk for departure.
translations.idiomatic: After Wugulun Qingshou's force was routed and no relief came, the capital's plight grew desperate; Jinzhong secretly plotted with his trusted marshal's staff officer Wanyan Shigu to abandon the city and flee south, had his baggage readied, and fixed departure for dusk on the second day of the fifth month.

sentences.zh: 是日，承暉、盡忠會議於尚書省，承暉無奈盡忠何，徑歸家，召師姑問之，知將以其夜出奔，乃先殺師姑，然後仰藥而死。

translations.literal: That day Cheng Hui and Jinzhong met in council at the Ministry; Cheng could do nothing about Jinzhong, went straight home, summoned Shigu and questioned him, learned that they would flee that night, first had Shigu executed, then took poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: That day Cheng and Jinzhong met at the Ministry; powerless to stop him, Cheng went home, questioned Shigu, learned of the night's flight, had Shigu executed, then took poison and died.

sentences.zh: 是日，凡在中都妃嬪，聞盡忠出奔，皆束裝至通玄門。

translations.literal: That day all the consorts in the Central Capital, hearing that Jinzhong was fleeing, packed their baggage and came to Tongxuan Gate.
translations.idiomatic: That day every consort still in the Central Capital, hearing of Jinzhong's flight, packed up and gathered at Tongxuan Gate.

sentences.zh: 盡忠謂之曰：「我當先出，與諸妃啟途。

translations.literal: Jinzhong told them, "I shall go out first and open the way for you ladies."
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhong told them, "I will go ahead first and clear the road for you."

sentences.zh: 」諸妃以為信然。

translations.literal: " The consorts believed him.
translations.idiomatic: " The consorts took him at his word.

sentences.zh: 盡忠乃與愛妾及所親者先出城，不復顧矣。

translations.literal: Jinzhong then left the city first with his favorite concubine and intimates, never looking back.
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhong then slipped out first with his favorite concubine and close followers, never looking back.

sentences.zh: 中都遂不守。

translations.literal: The Central Capital could no longer be held.
translations.idiomatic: The Central Capital fell.

sentences.zh: 盡忠行至中山，謂所親曰：」若與諸妃偕來，我輩豈能至此！」

translations.literal: When Jinzhong reached Zhongshan he told his intimates, "Had we come with the consorts, how could we have gotten this far!"
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Zhongshan, Jinzhong told his companions, "If we had brought the consorts along, we would never have made it this far!"

sentences.zh: 盡忠至南京，宣宗釋不問棄中都事，仍以為平章政事。

translations.literal: When Jinzhong reached Nanjing, Xuanzong pardoned him for abandoning the Central Capital and again appointed him grand councilor.
translations.idiomatic: At Nanjing, Xuanzong overlooked his abandonment of the Central Capital and restored him as grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 盡忠言：「記注之官，奏事不當回避，可令左右司官兼之。

translations.literal: Jinzhong said, "The record-keeping officials should not withdraw when matters are reported; the left and right secretariat directors may be ordered to hold the posts concurrently."
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhong proposed, "Record-keepers ought not to withdraw when business is discussed; let the left and right secretariat directors hold those posts as well."

sentences.zh: 」宣宗以為然。

translations.literal: " Xuanzong agreed.
translations.idiomatic: " Xuanzong approved.

sentences.zh: 盡忠奏應奉翰林文字完顏素蘭可為近侍局。

translations.literal: Jinzhong memorialized that Wanyan Sulan, a Hanlin attendant for imperial composition, was fit for the Palace Attendants Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhong recommended Wanyan Sulan, a Hanlin attendant for imperial composition, for appointment to the Palace Attendants Bureau.

sentences.zh: 宣宗曰：「近侍局例注本局人及宮中出身，雜以他色，恐或不和。

translations.literal: Xuanzong said, "The Palace Attendants Bureau is usually staffed from its own ranks and palace-born men; mixing in outsiders may cause discord."
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong replied, "That bureau is usually filled from its own staff and men raised in the palace; outsiders may upset its harmony."

sentences.zh: 」盡忠曰：「若給使左右，可止注本局人。

translations.literal: " Jinzhong said, "If they merely attend at one's side, one may limit appointments to bureau men."
translations.idiomatic: " Jinzhong said, "For mere personal attendance, bureau men alone would suffice."

sentences.zh: 既令預政，固宜慎選。

translations.literal: Since they are to take part in government, selection should indeed be careful.
translations.idiomatic: If they are to share in government, the choice must be careful.

sentences.zh: 」宣宗曰：「何謂預政？

translations.literal: " Xuanzong said, "What do you mean by taking part in government?"
translations.idiomatic: " Xuanzong asked, "What do you mean by sharing in government?"

sentences.zh: 」盡忠曰：「中外之事得議論訪察，即為預政矣。

translations.literal: " Jinzhong said, "When one may discuss and investigate affairs within and without the court, that is taking part in government."
translations.idiomatic: " Jinzhong answered, "Once they may discuss and investigate court and outside affairs, they are already in government."

sentences.zh: 」宣宗曰：「自世宗、章宗朝許察外事，非自朕始也。

translations.literal: " Xuanzong said, "Since the reigns of Shizong and Zhangzong they have been allowed to observe outside affairs; this did not begin with me."
translations.idiomatic: " Xuanzong said, "Shizong and Zhangzong already allowed them to watch outside affairs; I did not begin this."

sentences.zh: 如請謁營私，擬除不當，台諫不職，非近侍體察，何由知之？

translations.literal: When men seek audiences for private gain, appointments are improper, or the censorate fails in its duty—without palace attendants to observe, how could one know?"
translations.idiomatic: When men lobby for private ends, appointments go wrong, or the censorate neglects its duty—without palace attendants to see it, how would I know?"

sentences.zh: 」盡忠乃謝罪。

translations.literal: " Jinzhong then apologized.
translations.idiomatic: " Jinzhong apologized.

sentences.zh: 參政德升繼之曰：「固當慎選其人。

translations.literal: Vice Grand Councilor Desheng followed, saying, "One should indeed choose such men with care."
translations.idiomatic: Vice Grand Councilor Desheng added, "The men chosen should indeed be scrutinized with care."

sentences.zh: 」宣宗曰：「朕於庶官曷嘗不慎，有外似可用而實無才力者，視之若忠孝而包藏悖逆者。

translations.literal: " Xuanzong said, "Have I ever been careless with ordinary officials? Some seem usable outwardly yet lack real ability; some look loyal and filial yet harbor rebellion."
translations.idiomatic: " Xuanzong said, "When have I not been careful with ordinary officials? Some look capable yet lack real talent; some seem loyal yet conceal treachery."

sentences.zh: 蒲察七斤以刺史立功，驟升顯貴，輒懷異志。

translations.literal: Pucha Qijin won merit as a prefect, was suddenly raised to high rank, and at once harbored disloyal intent.
translations.idiomatic: Pucha Qijin won distinction as a prefect, was suddenly elevated, and soon turned disloyal.

sentences.zh: 蒲鮮萬奴委以遼東，乃複肆亂。

translations.literal: Puxian Wannu was entrusted with Liaodong and again ran riot.
translations.idiomatic: Puxian Wannu was entrusted with Liaodong and again plunged the region into chaos.

sentences.zh: 知人之難如此，朕敢輕乎！

translations.literal: Knowing men is this difficult—how dare I be careless!"
translations.idiomatic: To know men is this hard—how could I be careless!"

sentences.zh: 眾以蒲察五斤為公幹，乃除副使。

translations.literal: The multitude praised Pucha Wujin as upright and capable, so he was appointed deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Because many praised Pucha Wujin as upright and capable, he was made a deputy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 眾以斜烈為淳直，乃用為提點。

translations.literal: The multitude held Xielie to be honest and straightforward, so he was used as an intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Because many considered Xielie honest and plainspoken, he was made an intendant.

sentences.zh: 若烏古論石虎，乃汝等共舉之，朕豈不盡心哉！

translations.literal: As for Wugulun Shihu—it was you who jointly recommended him; have I not done my utmost!"
translations.idiomatic: Take Wugulun Shihu—you yourselves recommended him; have I not tried my utmost!"

sentences.zh: 」德 升曰：「比來訪察，開決河堤，水損田禾等，複之皆不實。

translations.literal: " Desheng said, "In recent investigations, reports of breaching dikes and flood damage to fields and crops have all proved false on review."
translations.idiomatic: " Desheng said, "Recent investigations—reports of dike breaches and flooded fields—have all proved false on reinspection."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「朕自今不敢問若輩，外間事皆不知，朕幹何事，但終日默坐聽汝等所為矣。

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "From now on I dare not question you people; I know nothing of outside affairs—what am I to do but sit in silence all day listening to whatever you do?"
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Hereafter I dare not question you at all; knowing nothing of the outside world, what can I do but sit silent all day and listen to whatever you decide?"

sentences.zh: 方朕有過，汝等不諫，今乃面訐，此豈為臣之義哉！

translations.literal: When I err you do not remonstrate, yet now you reproach me to my face—is this the duty of a minister!"
translations.idiomatic: When I err you offer no remonstrance, yet now you rebuke me to my face—is this how ministers should behave!"

sentences.zh: 」德升亦謝罪。

translations.literal: " Desheng also apologized.
translations.idiomatic: " Desheng apologized as well.

sentences.zh: 紇石烈執中之誅，近侍局嘗先事啟之，遂以為功，陰秉朝政。

translations.literal: In the execution of Heshilie Zhizhong the Palace Attendants Bureau had first reported the matter and claimed the merit, then secretly held court power.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Attendants Bureau had tipped off the court before Heshilie Zhizhong was executed, claimed the credit, and thereafter wielded secret influence over government.

sentences.zh: 高琪托此輩以自固。

translations.literal: Gao Qi relied on these men to secure himself.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Qi leaned on them to entrench his own power.

sentences.zh: 及盡忠、德升面責，愈無所忌。

translations.literal: After Jinzhong and Desheng rebuked them to their faces, they became all the more unafraid.
translations.idiomatic: After Jinzhong and Desheng rebuked them openly, they grew bolder still.

sentences.zh: 未幾，德升罷相，盡忠下獄，自是以後，中外蔽隔，以至於亡。

translations.literal: Before long Desheng was dismissed from the councilorship and Jinzhong was imprisoned; from then on court and country were cut off from each other, until the dynasty perished.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Desheng was removed from office and Jinzhong thrown into prison; thereafter court and country were walled off from one another until the dynasty fell.

sentences.zh: 盡忠與高琪素不相能，疑宣宗頗疏己，高琪間之。

translations.literal: Jinzhong and Gao Qi had long been incompatible; Jinzhong suspected that Xuanzong was rather distant toward him, and Gao Qi sowed discord between them.
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhong and Gao Qi had never gotten along; Jinzhong suspected the emperor was cooling toward him, and Gao Qi widened the rift.

sentences.zh: 其兄吾裏也為許州監酒，秩滿，求調南京。

translations.literal: His elder brother Wuliye was wine supervisor of Xuzhou; when his term ended he sought transfer to Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Wuliye, wine supervisor of Xuzhou, sought a transfer to Nanjing when his term ended.

sentences.zh: 盡忠與吾裏也語及中都事，曰：「邇來上頗疏我，此高琪所為也。

translations.literal: Jinzhong spoke with Wuliye about affairs at the Central Capital, saying, "Lately the emperor has been rather distant toward me—this is Gao Qi's doing."
translations.idiomatic: Speaking with Wuliye about the Central Capital, Jinzhong said, "The emperor has grown distant toward me lately—Gao Qi is behind it."

sentences.zh: 若再主兵，必不置此，胡沙虎之事，孰為為之！

translations.literal: If I again command the army, this will surely not be allowed—who was it that brought about the affair of Hu Shahu!"
translations.idiomatic: If I take command again, he will never allow it—who do you think engineered the Hu Shahu affair!"

sentences.zh: 」吾裏也曰：「然。

translations.literal: " Wuliye said, "Indeed."
translations.idiomatic: " Wuliye agreed, "Indeed."

sentences.zh: 」九月，尚書省奏：「遙授武寧軍節度副使徒單吾典告盡忠謀逆。

translations.literal: " In the ninth month the Ministry memorialized, "The remotely appointed deputy military commissioner of the Wuning Army, Tushan Wudian, reports that Jinzhong plots rebellion."
translations.idiomatic: " In the ninth month the Ministry reported that Tushan Wudian, remotely appointed deputy military commissioner of the Wuning Army, accused Jinzhong of plotting rebellion.

sentences.zh: 」上憮然曰：「朕何負彖多，彼棄中都，凡祖宗禦容及道陵諸妃皆不顧，獨與其妾偕來，此固有罪。

translations.literal: " The emperor said in distress, "What wrong have I done Suoduo? He abandoned the Central Capital, left the imperial portraits of the ancestors and all the consorts of Daoling, and came south with only his concubine—this is guilt in itself."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said bitterly, "What have I done to Suoduo? He abandoned the Central Capital, left the ancestral portraits and every consort of Daoling, and fled south with only his concubine—that alone is guilt enough."

sentences.zh: 」乃命有司鞫治，問得與兄吾裏也相語事，遂並吾裏也誅之。

translations.literal: " He ordered the authorities to investigate; inquiry revealed his conversation with his brother Wuliye, and Wuliye was executed along with him.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered an investigation; under questioning the talk with his brother Wuliye came out, and Wuliye was executed with him.

sentences.zh: 僕散端

translations.literal: Pu Sanduan
translations.idiomatic: Pu Sanduan

sentences.zh: 泰和六年，詔大臣議伐宋，皆曰無足慮者。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taihe an edict ordered the great ministers to discuss attacking Song; all said there was nothing to worry about.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Taihe the court ordered the senior ministers to debate war with Song; all declared there was little to fear.

sentences.zh: 左丞相宗浩、參知政事賈鉉亦曰：「狗盜鼠竊，非舉兵也。

translations.literal: Left Grand Councilor Zonghao and Vice Grand Councilor Jia Xuan also said, "Dog thieves and rat pilferers—this is not grounds for raising an army."
translations.idiomatic: Left Grand Councilor Zonghao and Vice Grand Councilor Jia Xuan likewise said, "Petty raids and skirmishes do not warrant a full campaign."

sentences.zh: 」端曰：「小寇當晝伏夜出，豈敢白日列陳，犯靈璧、入渦口、攻壽春邪？

translations.literal: " Duan said, "Petty raiders should hide by day and strike by night—how would they dare array ranks in broad daylight, strike Lingbi, enter Wokou, and attack Shouchun?"
translations.idiomatic: " Duan replied, "Bandits hide by day and strike at night—how would they dare deploy in daylight, assault Lingbi, enter the Wo estuary, and attack Shouchun?"

sentences.zh: 此宋人欲多方誤我，不早為之所，一旦大舉入寇，將墮其計中。

translations.literal: The Song wish to mislead us on many fronts; if we do not deal with this early, when they launch a great invasion at once we shall fall into their trap."
translations.idiomatic: The Song mean to confuse us on many fronts; unless we act early, when they strike in force we will walk straight into their trap."

sentences.zh: 」上深然之。

translations.literal: " The emperor strongly agreed.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was deeply persuaded.

sentences.zh: 未幾，丁母憂，起複尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Before long he left office for his mother's mourning, then was recalled as left vice minister of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he resigned to mourn his mother, then was recalled as left vice minister of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 平章政事僕散揆伐宋，發兵南京，詔端行省，主留務。

translations.literal: Grand Councilor Pu Sanhui campaigned against Song and launched troops from Nanjing; an edict made Duan branch secretariat and put him in charge of remaining affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councilor Pu Sanhui marched against Song from Nanjing; Duan was made branch secretariat and left in charge of affairs at home.

sentences.zh: 僕散揆已渡淮，次盧州。

translations.literal: Pu Sanhui had crossed the Huai and halted at Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Pu Sanhui had crossed the Huai and encamped at Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 宋使皇甫拱奉書乞和，端奏其書。

translations.literal: The Song envoy Huangfu Gong presented a letter suing for peace; Duan memorialized the letter.
translations.idiomatic: The Song envoy Huangfu Gong brought a letter suing for peace; Duan forwarded it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 朝議諸道兵既進，疑宋以計緩師，詔端遣拱還宋。

translations.literal: Court discussion held that with troops from all circuits already advancing, Song might be using a stratagem to delay the army; an edict ordered Duan to send Gong back to Song.
translations.idiomatic: The court feared that with armies already marching, Song was merely stalling; Duan was ordered to send Gong back.

sentences.zh: 七年，僕散揆以暑雨班師，端還朝。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Pu Sanhui withdrew the army because of summer rains; Duan returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Pu Sanhui withdrew because of summer rains; Duan returned to court.

sentences.zh: 初，婦人阿魯不嫁為武衛軍士妻，生二女而寡，常托夢中言以惑眾，頗有驗，或以為神。

translations.literal: Earlier a woman named Arubu had married a guardsman of the Martial Guard, borne two daughters, and become a widow; she often claimed words spoken in dreams to beguile the crowd, and several proved true, so some took her for divine.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier a widow named Arubu, once wife of a Martial Guard soldier and mother of two daughters, often claimed messages from dreams that swayed crowds; several proved true, and some took her for a prophet.

sentences.zh: 乃自言夢中屢見白頭老父指其二女曰：「皆有福人也。

translations.literal: She then said that in dreams she repeatedly saw a white-haired old man point to her two daughters and say, "Both are women of fortune."
translations.idiomatic: She claimed that in dreams a white-haired old man repeatedly pointed to her daughters and said, "Both are destined for greatness."

sentences.zh: 若侍掖廷，必得皇嗣。

translations.literal: If they attend in the inner palace, they will surely bear the imperial heir."
translations.idiomatic: If they enter the inner palace, they will surely bear the imperial heir."

sentences.zh: 」是時，章宗在位久，皇子未立，端請納之。

translations.literal: " At that time Zhangzong had long reigned and no heir had been established; Duan requested that they be taken in.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhangzong had long reigned without an heir; Duan urged that the daughters be brought into the palace.

sentences.zh: 章宗從之。

translations.literal: Zhangzong followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangzong agreed.

sentences.zh: 既而京師久不雨，阿魯不復言：「夢見白頭老父使己祈雨，三日必大澍足。

translations.literal: Before long the capital had long been without rain; Arubu again said, "In a dream the white-haired old man ordered me to pray for rain; within three days there will be a great downpour."
translations.idiomatic: When drought lingered over the capital, Arubu claimed again, "The white-haired old man in my dream told me to pray for rain; within three days there will be a great downpour."

sentences.zh: 」過三日雨不降，章宗疑其誕妄，下有司鞫問，阿魯不引伏。

translations.literal: " After three days no rain fell; Zhangzong suspected deception, ordered the authorities to investigate, and Arubu would not confess.
translations.idiomatic: " Three days passed without rain; Zhangzong suspected fraud, ordered an inquiry, and Arubu would not confess.

sentences.zh: 詔讓端曰：「昔者所奏，今其若何？

translations.literal: An edict reproached Duan, saying, "What of your former memorial—how stands it now?"
translations.idiomatic: An edict rebuked Duan: "What of your former recommendation—how does it look now?"

sentences.zh: 後人謂朕信其妖妄，實由卿啟其端，倪郁於予懷，念之難置。

translations.literal: Later men will say I believed her sorcery—it was really you who opened the way; the matter weighs on my mind and is hard to set aside.
translations.idiomatic: Later men will say I believed her sorcery—you opened the way; the matter weighs on my mind and will not leave it.

sentences.zh: 其循省於往咎，思善補於將來。

translations.literal: Reflect on past faults and think how to make good amends in what is to come.
translations.idiomatic: Reflect on past errors and find ways to make amends hereafter.

sentences.zh: 恪整乃心，式副朕意！

translations.literal: Keep your heart disciplined and fulfill my intent!"
translations.idiomatic: Keep your heart in order and meet my expectations!"

sentences.zh: 」端上表待罪，詔釋不問。

translations.literal: " Duan submitted a memorial awaiting punishment; an edict pardoned him without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: " Duan submitted a memorial accepting blame; the emperor pardoned him without further inquiry.

sentences.zh: 頃之，進拜平章政事，封申國公。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to grand councilor and enfeoffed as Duke of Shenguo.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made grand councilor and enfeoffed as Duke of Shenguo.

sentences.zh: 八年，宋人請盟，端遷一官。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the Song sought peace; Duan was promoted one rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, when Song sued for peace, Duan was promoted one rank.

sentences.zh: 貞祐二年五月，判南京留守，與河南統軍使長壽、按察轉運使王質表請南遷，凡三奏，宣宗意乃決。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year of Zhenyou, as acting garrison commissioner of Nanjing, together with Henan commander-in-chief Changshou and surveillance and transport commissioner Wang Zhi he memorialized requesting relocation south; after three memorials Xuanzong's mind was made up.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the second year of Zhenyou, acting Nanjing garrison commissioner, he joined Henan commander-in-chief Changshou and surveillance and transport commissioner Wang Zhi in three memorials urging relocation south, and Xuanzong's decision was set.

sentences.zh: 百官士庶皆言其不可，太學生趙昉等四百人上書極論利害，宣宗慰遣之，乃下詔遷都。

translations.literal: Officials and commoners all said it could not be done; four hundred students of the Imperial Academy led by Zhao Fang submitted a letter arguing the pros and cons at length; Xuanzong comforted and dismissed them, then issued an edict moving the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners alike protested; four hundred Imperial Academy students led by Zhao Fang submitted a long letter on the risks; Xuanzong comforted and dismissed them, then issued the edict relocating the capital.

sentences.zh: 明年，中都失守。

translations.literal: The next year the Central Capital fell.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the Central Capital was lost.

sentences.zh: 宣宗至南京，以端知開封府事。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong reached Nanjing he appointed Duan to administer Kaifeng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong reached Nanjing he put Duan in charge of Kaifeng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 頃之，為禦使大夫，無何，拜尚書左丞相。

translations.literal: Before long he became censor-in-chief; soon afterward he was appointed left grand councilor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became censor-in-chief; not long after he was made left grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 三年，兼樞密副使，未幾，進兼樞密使。

translations.literal: In the third year he was concurrently vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs; before long he was advanced to concurrent commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs; soon he was promoted to commissioner.

sentences.zh: 數月，以左丞相兼都元帥行省陝西，給親軍三十人、騎兵三百為衛，次子宿直將軍納坦出侍行。

translations.literal: Several months later, as left grand councilor and concurrently supreme commander with branch secretariat over Shaanxi, he was given thirty personal guards and three hundred cavalry as escort; his second son, Palace Duty General Nadan, attended him on the journey.
translations.idiomatic: Months later, as left grand councilor and supreme commander with charge of the Shaanxi branch secretariat, he was given thirty personal guards and three hundred cavalry; his second son Nadan, a palace duty general, accompanied him.

sentences.zh: 賜契紙勘同曰：「緩急有事，以此召卿。

translations.literal: He was granted matched contract papers saying, "In urgent matters use this to summon you."
translations.idiomatic: He received matched contract papers reading, "In any emergency, use this to summon you."

sentences.zh: 」端招遙領通遠軍節度使完顏狗兒即日來歸，奏遷知平涼府事，諸將聞之，莫不感激。

translations.literal: " Duan summoned the remotely appointed military commissioner of the Tongyuan Army, Wanyan Gou'er, who came over the same day; he memorialized to transfer him to administer Pingliang Prefecture; when the generals heard of it, none failed to be moved with gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: " Duan won over the remotely appointed Tongyuan military commissioner Wanyan Gou'er, who submitted the same day; Duan had him made prefect of Pingliang, and every general who heard of it was deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 遣納蘭伴僧招諭臨洮祇黎五族都管青覺兒、積石州章羅謁蘭冬及鐸精族都管阿令結、蘭州葩俄族都管汪三郎等，皆相繼內附。

translations.literal: He sent Nalan Banseng to win over Qingjiao'er, chief of the five Qili tribes of Lintao, Zhangluo Yelandong of Jishi Prefecture, Alingjie chief of the Duojing tribe, Wang Sanlang chief of the Pao'e tribe of Lanzhou, and others, who all submitted in succession.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Nalan Banseng to win over Qingjiao'er, head of the five Qili tribes of Lintao, Zhangluo Yelandong of Jishi, Alingjie of the Duojing tribe, Wang Sanlang of the Pao'e tribe of Lanzhou, and others, who submitted one after another.

sentences.zh: 汪三郎賜姓完顏，後為西方名將。

translations.literal: Wang Sanlang was granted the surname Wanyan and later became a famous general of the west.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sanlang was granted the surname Wanyan and later became a renowned western commander.

sentences.zh: 四年，以疾請致仕，不許，遣近侍與太醫診視。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he requested retirement on grounds of illness; this was not granted, and palace attendants and imperial physicians were sent to examine him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he asked to retire for illness; the request was denied, and palace attendants and imperial physicians were sent to examine him.

sentences.zh: 端雖癃老，凡朝廷使至，必遠迓，宴勞不懈，故讒構不果行。

translations.literal: Though Duan was infirm with age, whenever a court envoy arrived he always went far to meet him and entertained him without slackening, so slanders did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Though aged and infirm, whenever a court envoy arrived Duan went far to meet him and entertained him tirelessly, so slander failed to take hold.

sentences.zh: 宣宗聞之，詔自今專使酒三行別於儀門，他事經過者一見而止。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong heard of it, an edict said that from now on special envoys might be given three rounds of wine and farewell at the ceremonial gate, while others passing through on business should be received once only.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of this, Xuanzong ruled that henceforth special envoys might be honored with three rounds of wine at the ceremonial gate, while others merely passing through should receive a single audience.

sentences.zh: 初，同、華舊屯陝西軍及河南步騎九千餘人，皆隸陝州宣撫副使永錫，端奏：「潼關之西，皆陝西地，請此軍隸行省，緩急可使。

translations.literal: Earlier more than nine thousand infantry and cavalry of the Shaanxi army formerly stationed at Tong and Hua and the Henan foot and horse were all under Shaanzhou pacification deputy Yongxi; Duan memorialized, saying, "West of Tong Pass all is Shaanxi territory; I request that this army be placed under the branch secretariat so it may be used in emergencies."
translations.idiomatic: More than nine thousand Shaanxi troops once posted at Tong and Hua and Henan infantry and cavalry had all been under Shaanzhou pacification deputy Yongxi; Duan argued that west of Tong Pass lay Shaanxi and asked that these forces be attached to his branch secretariat for use in emergencies.

sentences.zh: 」朝廷從之。

translations.literal: " The court approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 及大元兵入潼關，永錫坐誅，而罪不及端。

translations.literal: When the Great Yuan army entered Tong Pass, Yongxi was executed for it, but blame did not reach Duan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yuan army broke through Tong Pass, Yongxi was executed, but Duan was not implicated.

sentences.zh: 耿端義

translations.literal: Geng Duanyi
translations.idiomatic: Geng Duanyi

sentences.zh: 耿端義，字忠嗣，博州博平人。

translations.literal: Geng Duanyi, courtesy name Zhongsi, was a native of Boping in Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Duanyi, whose courtesy name was Zhongsi, came from Boping in Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 大定二十八年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-eighth year of Dading.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the twenty-eighth year of Dading.

sentences.zh: 調滑州軍事判官，曆上洛縣令，安化、順義軍節度判官，補尚書省令史，除汾陽軍節度副使，改都轉運司戶籍判官，轉太常博士，遷太常丞兼秘書郎，再除左司員外郎，曆太常少卿兼吏部員外郎，同修國史，戶部郎中，河北東路按察副使，同知東平府事，充山東安撫使。

translations.literal: He was appointed military judge of Huazhou, served in succession as magistrate of Shangluo and as judge of the Anhua and Shunyi armies, entered the Secretariat as a clerk, was made deputy military commissioner of the Fenyang Army, transferred to household registration judge of the metropolitan transport commission, became an Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, rose to vice director of that court while concurrently secretary, was again made outer director of the Left Secretariat, served as vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices while concurrently outer director of the Personnel Bureau, helped compile the national history, became director of the Revenue Bureau, deputy surveillance commissioner of the Hebei East circuit, deputy prefect of Dongping, and pacification commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Posted as military judge of Huazhou, he served as magistrate of Shangluo and judge on the Anhua and Shunyi armies, entered the Secretariat, became deputy commissioner of the Fenyang army and household registration judge on the transport commission, rose through the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Left Secretariat, helped compile the national history, directed the Revenue Bureau, served as deputy surveillance commissioner on the Hebei East circuit and deputy prefect of Dongping, and was made pacification commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 宣宗判汾陽軍，是時端義為副使。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong administered the Fenyang army, Duanyi was deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong held the Fenyang army, Duanyi served as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位，召見，訪問時事，遷翰林侍講學士兼戶部侍郎，未幾，拜參知政事。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong took the throne he was summoned, questioned on current affairs, promoted to Hanlin exposition academician and concurrently vice minister of Revenue, and before long made vice grand councilor.
translations.idiomatic: On Xuanzong's accession he was summoned, consulted on affairs of state, made Hanlin exposition academician and vice minister of Revenue, and soon afterward vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 貞祐二年，中都被圍，將帥皆不肯戰。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyou the Central Capital was besieged and the generals all refused to fight.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenyou, with the Central Capital besieged, the commanders refused to give battle.

sentences.zh: 端義奏曰：「今日之患，衛王啟之。

translations.literal: Duanyi memorialized, saying, "Today's calamity was begun by Prince Wei."
translations.idiomatic: Duanyi memorialized, "Today's disaster began with Prince Wei."

sentences.zh: 士卒縱不可使，城中軍官自都統至謀克不啻萬餘，遣此輩一出，或可以得志。

translations.literal: Though common soldiers may not be usable, the officers in the city from army directors down to mouke number no fewer than ten thousand; send these men out once and success may yet be achieved."
translations.idiomatic: Even if the rank and file cannot be relied on, more than ten thousand officers from army directors down to mouke remain in the city; send them out and the tide may yet turn."

sentences.zh: 」議竟不行。

translations.literal: " The proposal was never carried out.
translations.idiomatic: " The plan was never adopted.

sentences.zh: 中都解圍，端義請遷南京。

translations.literal: When the siege of the Central Capital was lifted, Duanyi requested relocation to Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: After the siege lifted, Duanyi urged moving the court to Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 既而僕散端三表皆言遷都事，宣宗意遂決。

translations.literal: Before long Pu Sanduan submitted three memorials on moving the capital, and Xuanzong's decision was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Pu Sanduan's three memorials on relocating the capital settled Xuanzong's mind.

sentences.zh: 是歲，薨。

translations.literal: That year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died that year.

sentences.zh: 宣宗輟朝，賻贈甚厚，遣使祭葬。

translations.literal: Xuanzong suspended court, gave lavish funeral gifts, and sent envoys to offer sacrifices at the burial.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong suspended court, granted lavish funeral gifts, and sent envoys to mourn at his burial.

sentences.zh: 李英，字子賢，其先遼陽人，徙益都。

translations.literal: Li Ying, courtesy name Zixian, was descended from Liaoyang people who had moved to Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ying, courtesy name Zixian, came of a family from Liaoyang that had settled in Yidu.

sentences.zh: 中明昌五年進士第，調淳化主簿、登州軍事判官、封丘令。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Mingchang, and was appointed registrar of Chunhua, military judge of Dengzhou, and magistrate of Fengqiu.
translations.idiomatic: He took the jinshi in the fifth year of Mingchang and served as registrar of Chunhua, military judge of Dengzhou, and magistrate of Fengqiu.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，服除，調通遠令。

translations.literal: After mourning his father and completing the mourning period, he was appointed magistrate of Tongyuan.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's mourning period ended, he was posted as magistrate of Tongyuan.

sentences.zh: 蕃部取民物不與直，攝之不時至，即掩捕之，論如法。

translations.literal: When frontier tribes took people's goods without fair payment and the summons did not bring them in time, he seized them in surprise raids and judged them according to law.
translations.idiomatic: When tribesmen took goods without paying fair value and failed to appear when summoned, he raided and arrested them and punished them by law.

sentences.zh: 補尚書省令史。

translations.literal: He entered the Secretariat as a clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a secretariat clerk.

sentences.zh: 大安三年，集三品以上官議兵事，英上疏曰：「軍旅必練習者，朮虎高琪、烏古孫兀屯、納蘭𠇗頭、抹撚盡忠先朝嘗任使，可與商略。

translations.literal: In the third year of Da'an officials of the third rank and above were assembled to discuss military affairs; Ying submitted a memorial, saying, "For armies that must be drilled, Tuhu Gao Qi, Wugusun Wutun, Nalan Zhantou, and Monian Jinzhong were employed in the previous reign and may be consulted."
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Da'an the court gathered officials of the third rank and above to discuss war; Ying wrote, "For forces that must be trained, Tuhu Gao Qi, Wugusun Wutun, Nalan Zhantou, and Monian Jinzhong all served under the previous emperor and should be consulted."

sentences.zh: 餘者紛紛，恐誤大計。

translations.literal: The rest are numerous and may confuse the great plan."
translations.idiomatic: The rest are too many and may confuse strategy."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「比來增築城郭，修完樓櫓，事勢可知，山東、河北不大其聲援，則京師為孤城矣。

translations.literal: " He also said, "Of late walls and towers have been built and repaired—the trend is clear; if Shandong and Hebei do not raise loud support, the capital will stand as a lone city."
translations.idiomatic: " He added, "The recent rush to build walls and towers shows the trend: unless Shandong and Hebei rally strongly, the capital will stand alone."

sentences.zh: 」不報。

translations.literal: " There was no response.
translations.idiomatic: " The court did not reply.

sentences.zh: 除吏部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed chief clerk of the Personnel Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was made chief clerk of the Personnel Bureau.

sentences.zh: 貞祐初，攝左司都事，遷監察御史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyou he acted as chief clerk of the Left Secretariat, then was promoted to investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenyou he served as acting chief clerk of the Left Secretariat, then became an investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 右副元帥朮虎高琪辟為經歷官，乃上書高琪曰：「中都之有居庸，猶秦之崤、函，蜀之劍門也。

translations.literal: Right Deputy Commander Tuhu Gao Qi recruited him as staff officer; he then wrote to Gao Qi, saying, "For the Central Capital to have Juyong is like Qin having Xiao and Han, or Shu having Jianmen."
translations.idiomatic: Right Deputy Commander Tuhu Gao Qi took him onto his staff; Ying wrote to him, "Juyong to the Central Capital is what Xiao and Han were to Qin and Jianmen to Shu."

sentences.zh: 邇者撤居庸兵，我勢遂去。

translations.literal: Lately the Juyong garrison was withdrawn and our strength departed.
translations.idiomatic: Recently the Juyong garrison was withdrawn and our strategic position was lost.

sentences.zh: 今土豪守之，朝廷當遣官節制，失此不圖，忠義之士，將轉為他矣。

translations.literal: Now local strongmen hold it; the court should send officials to control them—if this is not planned for, loyal men will turn elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Local strongmen now hold it; the court should send officers to command them—neglect this and loyal men will go over to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「可鎮撫宣德、德興餘民，使之從戎。

translations.literal: " He also said, "The remaining people of Xuande and Dexing may be pacified and made to take up arms."
translations.idiomatic: " He also urged pacifying the survivors of Xuande and Dexing and enrolling them in the army.

sentences.zh: 所在自有宿藏，足以取給，是國家不費鬥糧尺帛，坐收所失之關隘也。

translations.literal: Every place has stored supplies enough to provision them—thus the state spends no bushel of grain or foot of silk yet recovers the lost passes.
translations.idiomatic: Local stores can supply them, so the state need spend no grain or cloth yet recover the lost passes.

sentences.zh: 居庸咫尺，都之北門，而不能衛護，英實恥之。

translations.literal: Juyong lies within a stone's throw, the capital's northern gate, yet cannot be guarded—Ying is truly shamed.
translations.idiomatic: Juyong lies at the capital's very northern gate, yet we cannot hold it—Ying felt deep shame.

sentences.zh: 」高琪奏其書，即除尚書工部員外郎，充宣差都提控，居庸等關隘悉隸焉。
