translations.literal: " Gao Qi memorialized the letter; Ying was at once made outer director of the Works Bureau of the Secretariat and appointed imperial commissioner and overall controller, with Juyong and other passes all under him.
translations.idiomatic: " Gao Qi forwarded the letter; Ying was made outer director of the Works Bureau and imperial commissioner over Juyong and the other passes.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，乘夜與壯士李雄、郭仲元、郭興祖等四百九十人出城，緣西山進至佛岩寺。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year, by night he left the city with four hundred ninety brave men including Li Xiong, Guo Zhongyuan, and Guo Xingzu, followed the western hills to Foyan Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year he slipped out at night with four hundred ninety men including Li Xiong, Guo Zhongyuan, and Guo Xingzu and made his way along the western hills to Foyan Temple.

sentences.zh: 令李雄等下山招募軍民，旬日得萬餘人。

translations.literal: He ordered Li Xiong and others down the mountain to recruit soldiers and civilians; within ten days they gathered more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Li Xiong and others to recruit troops and civilians; within ten days they raised more than ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 擇眾所推服者領之，詭稱土豪，時時出戰。

translations.literal: He chose those the crowd respected to lead them, falsely called them local strongmen, and from time to time gave battle.
translations.idiomatic: He put trusted local leaders in command, passed them off as militia chiefs, and skirmished regularly.

sentences.zh: 被創，召還。

translations.literal: Wounded, he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Wounded in action, he was recalled to court.

sentences.zh: 遷翰林待制，因獻十策，其大概謂：「居中土以鎮四方，委親賢以守中都，立潘屏以固關隘，集人力以防不虞，養馬力以助軍威，愛禾稼以結民心，明賞罰以勸百官，選守令以複郡縣，並州縣以省民力。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Hanlin attendant and presented ten policies, in summary: "Hold the central lands to command the four quarters; entrust kinsmen and worthies to guard the Central Capital; establish screens to secure the passes; gather manpower against surprise; raise horses to strengthen the army; cherish the harvest to bind the people's hearts; clarify rewards and punishments to encourage officials; choose prefects and magistrates to recover the commanderies and counties; merge counties to spare the people's strength."
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Hanlin attendant, he offered ten policies: hold the heartland to command the realm; entrust kin and worthies to guard the Central Capital; fortify the passes; gather manpower against surprise; raise horses for the army; protect the harvest to win the people; clarify rewards and punishments; choose able local officials to recover the counties; merge districts to spare the populace.

sentences.zh: 」頗施行之。

translations.literal: " Many were put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: " Many of these measures were adopted.

sentences.zh: 宣宗南遷，與左諫議大夫把胡魯俱為御前經歷官。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong moved south, Ying and Left Remonstrance Grandee Ba Hulu both served as staff officers before the imperial presence.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong moved south, Ying and Left Remonstrance Grandee Ba Hulu served together on the imperial staff.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「扈從軍馬，朕自總之，事有利害，可因近侍局以聞。

translations.literal: An edict said, "The escort troops and horses I shall command myself; when affairs have benefit or harm, you may report through the Palace Attendants Bureau."
translations.idiomatic: An edict read, "I shall command the escort forces myself; report any matter of consequence through the Palace Attendants Bureau."

sentences.zh: 」宣宗次真定，以英為國子祭酒，充宣差提控隴右邊事。

translations.literal: " When Xuanzong halted at Zhending he made Ying director of the Imperial Academy and appointed him imperial commissioner to control Longyou frontier affairs.
translations.idiomatic: " At Zhending, Xuanzong made Ying director of the Imperial Academy and imperial commissioner for the Longyou frontier.

sentences.zh: 無何，召為御史中丞。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned as censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was recalled as censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 英言：「兵興以來，百務皆弛，其要在於激濁揚清，獎進人材耳。

translations.literal: Ying said, "Since war began every affair has slackened; the key lies in stirring the clear and sinking the turbid and advancing talent."
translations.idiomatic: Ying said, "Since the wars began every branch of government has slackened; the essential task is to reward the worthy, purge the corrupt, and advance talent."

sentences.zh: 近年改定四善、二十七最之法，徒為虛文。

translations.literal: In recent years the revised law of four virtues and twenty-seven excellences is mere empty form.
translations.idiomatic: The recent revision of the four virtues and twenty-seven excellences rating system has become empty paperwork.

sentences.zh: 大定間，數遣使者分道考察廉能，當時號為得人。

translations.literal: During Dading envoys were repeatedly sent on separate routes to examine integrity and ability, and the age was praised for gaining the right men.
translations.idiomatic: Under Dading the court repeatedly sent envoys to assess officials for integrity and ability, and the age was praised for finding the right men.

sentences.zh: 願改前日徒設之文，遵大定已試之效，庶幾人人自勵，為國家用矣。

translations.literal: I wish to change the empty forms of recent days and follow the tested effect of Dading, so that each man may spur himself and serve the state."
translations.idiomatic: I urge that we abandon today's empty forms and return to Dading's proven methods, so that every man may strive on his own account for the state's service."

sentences.zh: 」宣宗嘉納之。

translations.literal: " Xuanzong commended and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: " Xuanzong praised and accepted the proposal.

sentences.zh: 自兵興以來，亟用官爵為賞，程陳僧敗官軍于龕穀，遣偽統制董九招西關堡都統王狗兒，狗兒立殺之。

translations.literal: Since the wars began offices and ranks have been used repeatedly as rewards; the monk Cheng Chen defeated government troops at Kangu and sent the false commander Dong Jiu to win over Wang Gou'er, garrison commander of Xiguan Fort, who at once killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Since the wars began the court has showered offices and ranks as rewards; the monk Cheng Chen routed government troops at Kangu and sent the false commander Dong Jiu to win over Wang Gou'er, commander of Xiguan Fort, who killed him on the spot.

sentences.zh: 詔除通遠軍節度使，加榮祿大夫，賜姓完顏氏。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him military commissioner of the Tongyuan Army, granted the title Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and bestowed the surname Wanyan.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made him military commissioner of the Tongyuan army, granted him Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and bestowed the surname Wanyan.

sentences.zh: 英言：「名器不可以假人，上恩以難得為貴。

translations.literal: Ying said, "Titles and offices must not be lent to others; imperial favor is precious because it is hard to obtain."
translations.idiomatic: Ying objected, "Honors must not be handed out lightly; imperial favor is precious because it is rare."

sentences.zh: 比來醲於用賞，實駭聞聽。

translations.literal: Of late rewards have been lavished so heavily as to shock all who hear.
translations.idiomatic: Lately rewards have been showered so freely as to shock everyone who hears of it.

sentences.zh: 帑藏不足，惟恃爵命，今又輕之，何以使人？

translations.literal: The treasury is insufficient and we rely only on rank and commission; now these too are cheapened—how can we move men?"
translations.idiomatic: The treasury is empty and we rely on rank alone; now even that is debased—how can we command loyalty?"

sentences.zh: 伏見蘭州西關堡守將王狗兒向以微勞，既蒙甄錄，頃者堅守關城，誘殺賊使，論其忠節，誠有可嘉。

translations.literal: I observe that Wang Gou'er, defender of Xiguan Fort at Lanzhou, for slight merit was already selected and recorded; recently he held the pass firmly and lured and killed the enemy envoy—in loyalty and constancy he is truly praiseworthy.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gou'er of Xiguan Fort at Lanzhou earned recognition for modest service; he held the pass, lured and killed the enemy envoy, and in loyalty deserves praise.

sentences.zh: 若官之五品，命以一州，亦無負矣。

translations.literal: A fifth-rank office and appointment to a prefecture would not be excessive.
translations.idiomatic: A fifth-rank post and a prefecture would be reward enough.

sentences.zh: 急於勸獎，遂擢節鉞，加階二品，賜以國姓，若取蘭州，又將何以待之？

translations.literal: Eager to encourage him, you have raised him to military commissioner, advanced him two ranks, and granted the imperial surname—if he takes Lanzhou, how will you reward him then?"
translations.idiomatic: In haste to reward him you made him a military commissioner, raised him two ranks, and gave him the imperial surname—if he captures Lanzhou, what reward remains?"

sentences.zh: 陝西名將項背相望，曹記僧、包長壽、東永昌、徒單醜兒、郭祿大皆其著者。

translations.literal: Famous generals of Shaanxi stand one behind another—Cao Jiseng, Bao Changshou, Dong Yongchang, Tushan Chou'er, and Guo Luda are among the notable.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi's famous commanders are legion—Cao Jiseng, Bao Changshou, Dong Yongchang, Tushan Chou'er, and Guo Luda among the foremost.

sentences.zh: 狗兒藐然賤卒，一朝處眾人之右，為統領之官，恐眾望不厭，難得其死力。

translations.literal: Gou'er is a mere lowly soldier; in one morning he is placed above the multitude as a commanding officer—fearing that public expectation will not be satisfied, it will be hard to win his utmost effort."
translations.idiomatic: Gou'er is a common soldier raised overnight above veteran commanders—many will resent it, and he may not win their wholehearted service."

sentences.zh: 」宣宗以英奏示宰臣。

translations.literal: " Xuanzong showed Ying's memorial to the chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: " Xuanzong showed Ying's memorial to the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 宰臣奏：「狗兒奮發如此，賞以異恩，殆不為過。

translations.literal: The chief ministers memorialized, "Gou'er has exerted himself thus; to reward him with special favor is scarcely excessive."
translations.idiomatic: The ministers replied, "Gou'er has shown such zeal; an extraordinary reward is hardly excessive."

sentences.zh: 」上然其言。

translations.literal: " The emperor agreed with them.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor accepted their view.

sentences.zh: 中都久圍，丞相承暉遣人以礬寫奏告急。

translations.literal: The Central Capital was long besieged; Grand Councilor Cheng Hui sent men to write urgent memorials in alum fluid.
translations.idiomatic: With the Central Capital long besieged, Grand Councilor Cheng Hui sent couriers bearing urgent memorials written in alum ink.

sentences.zh: 詔元帥左監軍永錫、左都監烏古論慶壽將兵，英收河間清、滄義軍自清州督糧運救中都。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Left Army Supervisor Yongxi and Left Army Director Wugulun Qingshou to lead troops; Ying was to gather the volunteer armies of Hejian, Qing, and Cang and from Qingzhou supervise grain transport to relieve the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yongxi and Wugulun Qingshou were ordered to march; Ying was to rally the Hejian, Qing, and Cang volunteer forces and convoy grain from Qingzhou to relieve the Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 英至大名，得兵數萬，馭眾素無紀律。

translations.literal: Ying reached Daming and gathered tens of thousands of troops, but in commanding the multitude he had never maintained discipline.
translations.idiomatic: At Daming Ying assembled tens of thousands of men but had never enforced discipline among them.

sentences.zh: 貞祐三年三月十六日，英被酒，與大元兵遇於霸州北，大敗，盡失所運糧。

translations.literal: On the sixteenth day of the third month in the third year of Zhenyou Ying was drunk; he met the Great Yuan army north of Bazhou, was utterly defeated, and lost all the grain he was transporting.
translations.idiomatic: On the sixteenth day of the third month of the third year of Zhenyou, drunk, Ying met the Yuan army north of Bazhou, was routed, and lost all his supplies.

sentences.zh: 英死，士卒殲焉。

translations.literal: Ying died and the soldiers were annihilated.
translations.idiomatic: Ying was killed and his force wiped out.

sentences.zh: 慶壽、永錫軍聞之，皆潰歸。

translations.literal: The armies of Qingshou and Yongxi, hearing of it, all collapsed and returned.
translations.idiomatic: On hearing the news, the forces of Qingshou and Yongxi broke and fled home.

sentences.zh: 五月，中都不守，宣宗猶加恩，贈通奉大夫，諡剛貞，官護葬事，錄用其子雲。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the Central Capital fell; Xuanzong still showed favor, posthumously granted Grand Master of the Palace, posthumous title Gangzhen, ordered officials to oversee the funeral, and employed his son Yun.
translations.idiomatic: When the Central Capital fell in the fifth month, Xuanzong still honored him posthumously as Grand Master of the Palace with the name Gangzhen (Steadfast and Upright), ordered an official funeral, and employed his son Yun.

sentences.zh: 孛朮魯德裕

translations.literal: Bei Pailu Deyu
translations.idiomatic: Bei Pailu Deyu

sentences.zh: 孛朮魯德裕，本名蒲剌都，隆安路猛安人。

translations.literal: Bei Pailu Deyu, original name Puladu, was a meng'an man of the Long'an circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Bei Pailu Deyu, originally named Puladu, came from a meng'an household of the Long'an circuit.

sentences.zh: 補樞密院尚書省令史，右三部檢法、監察御史，遷少府監丞。

translations.literal: He entered the Bureau of Military Affairs and Secretariat as a clerk, served as inspector of the Right Three Departments and as investigating censor, and was promoted to vice director of the Palace Workshops.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a clerk in the Bureau of Military Affairs and Secretariat, as inspector of the Right Three Departments and investigating censor, then became vice director of the Palace Workshops.

sentences.zh: 明昌末，修北邊壕塹，立堡塞，以勞進官三階，授大理正。

translations.literal: At the end of Mingchang he repaired northern frontier trenches and ditches and established forts; for his labor he was promoted three ranks and appointed chief judge of the Court of Review.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Mingchang he built northern frontier trenches and forts; for this labor he was promoted three ranks and made chief judge of the Court of Review.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，起複廣寧治中，曆順州、濱州刺史。

translations.literal: He left office for his mother's mourning, was recalled as administrator of Guangning, and served in succession as prefect of Shunzhou and Binzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his mother he was recalled as administrator of Guangning and served as prefect of Shunzhou and Binzhou in turn.

sentences.zh: 坐前在順州市物虧直，遇赦，改刺沈州，累官北京路按察使、太子詹事、元帥左都監，遷左監軍兼監潢府路兵馬都總管。

translations.literal: For shortchanging goods while in Shunzhou he was punished, then pardoned and transferred to Shenzhou; he rose in succession to surveillance commissioner of the Northern Capital circuit, grand mentor of the heir apparent, and left army director of the commander-in-chief, then left army supervisor while concurrently supervising all horse and foot of the Huangfu circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Punished for shortchanging market goods in Shunzhou, then pardoned and posted to Shenzhou, he rose to surveillance commissioner of the Northern Capital, grand mentor of the heir apparent, left army director, and then left army supervisor overseeing all troops of the Huangfu circuit.

sentences.zh: 坐士馬物故多，及都統按帶私率官兵救護家屬，德裕蔽之，御史劾奏逮獄。

translations.literal: For many soldiers and horses lost in service, and because army director Wanyan Andai privately led troops to rescue his family while Deyu concealed it, the censorate impeached him and he was imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: When many men and horses were lost and army director Wanyan Andai privately led troops to rescue his family while Deyu covered for him, the censorate impeached him and he was jailed.

sentences.zh: 遇赦，謫甯海州刺史，稍遷泗州防禦使、武勝軍節度使。

translations.literal: He was pardoned, demoted to prefect of Ninghai, and later promoted to defense commissioner of Sizhou and military commissioner of the Wusheng Army.
translations.idiomatic: Pardoned, he was demoted to prefect of Ninghai, then promoted to defense commissioner of Sizhou and military commissioner of the Wusheng army.

sentences.zh: 貞祐二年，改知臨洮府事，兼陝西路副統軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyou he was transferred to administer Lintao Prefecture and concurrently made deputy commander of the Shaanxi circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenyou he governed Lintao Prefecture while serving as deputy commander of the Shaanxi circuit.

sentences.zh: 召為御史中丞，拜參知政事兼簽樞密院事，行省大名。

translations.literal: He was summoned as censor-in-chief, made vice grand councilor and concurrently signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs, with branch secretariat at Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as censor-in-chief, he became vice grand councilor and signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs with charge of the Daming branch secretariat.

sentences.zh: 詔發河北兵救中都。

translations.literal: An edict dispatched Hebei troops to relieve the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Hebei troops to relieve the Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 凡真定、中山、保、涿等兵，元帥左監軍永錫將之，大名、河間、清、滄、觀、霸、河南等兵，德裕將之，並護清、滄糧運。

translations.literal: The troops of Zhending, Zhongshan, Bao, Zhuo, and the like were led by Left Army Supervisor Yongxi; the troops of Daming, Hejian, Qing, Cang, Guan, Ba, Henan, and the like were led by Deyu, who also protected grain transport from Qing and Cang.
translations.idiomatic: Yongxi led the Zhending, Zhongshan, Bao, and Zhuo columns; Deyu led the Daming, Hejian, Qing, Cang, Guan, Ba, and Henan forces and also guarded grain convoys from Qing and Cang.

sentences.zh: 德裕不時發。

translations.literal: Deyu did not set out on time.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu failed to march on schedule.

sentences.zh: 及李英至霸州兵敗，糧盡亡失，坐弛慢兵期，責授沂州防禦使，尋知益都府事。

translations.literal: When Li Ying reached Bazhou and his army was defeated and all grain lost, Deyu was punished for slackness in the military schedule, demoted to defense commissioner of Yizhou, and soon appointed to administer Yidu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Ying's defeat at Bazhou and the loss of all supplies, Deyu was punished for missing the campaign deadline, demoted to defense commissioner of Yizhou, and soon put in charge of Yidu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 興定元年二月，卒。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Xingding he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second month of the first year of Xingding.

sentences.zh: 烏古論慶壽

translations.literal: Wugulun Qingshou
translations.idiomatic: Wugulun Qingshou

sentences.zh: 烏古論慶壽，河北西路猛安人，由知把書畫充奉禦，除近侍局直長，再轉本局使。

translations.literal: Wugulun Qingshou, a meng'an man of the Hebei West circuit, from keeper of paintings became an imperial attendant, was made director of the Palace Attendants Bureau, and later became commissioner of that bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Wugulun Qingshou, from a meng'an household of the Hebei West circuit, rose from keeper of paintings to imperial attendant, became director of the Palace Attendants Bureau, and later its commissioner.

sentences.zh: 禦邊有勞，進一階，賜金帶。

translations.literal: For merit on the frontier he was promoted one rank and granted a gold belt.
translations.idiomatic: For frontier service he was promoted one rank and given a gold belt.

sentences.zh: 泰和四年，遷本局提點。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taihe he was transferred to intendant of the bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Taihe he became intendant of the bureau.

sentences.zh: 是時，議開通州漕河，詔慶壽按視。

translations.literal: At that time the opening of the Tongzhou grain canal was under discussion; an edict ordered Qingshou to inspect it.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated opening the Tongzhou grain canal, Qingshou was ordered to inspect the project.

sentences.zh: 漕河成，賜銀一百五十兩、重幣十端。

translations.literal: When the canal was completed he was granted a hundred fifty taels of silver and ten lengths of heavy gifts.
translations.idiomatic: When the canal was finished he received a hundred fifty taels of silver and ten lengths of heavy brocade.

sentences.zh: 泰和六年，伐宋，從右副元帥完顏匡出唐鄧，為先鋒都統，賜禦弓二。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taihe, on the campaign against Song, he followed Right Deputy Commander Wanyan Kui through Tang and Deng as vanguard commander and was granted two imperial bows.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Taihe, campaigning against Song under Right Deputy Commander Wanyan Kui through Tang and Deng, he served as vanguard commander and received two imperial bows.

sentences.zh: 以騎兵八千攻下棗陽。

translations.literal: With eight thousand cavalry he captured Zaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He took Zaoyang with eight thousand cavalry.

sentences.zh: 頃之，完顏匡軍次白虎粒，遣都統完顏按帶取隨州，遣慶壽以兵五千扼赤岸，斷襄漢路。

translations.literal: Before long Wanyan Kui's army halted at Baihuli; he sent Army Director Wanyan Andai to take Suizhou and sent Qingshou with five thousand men to hold Chian and cut the Xiang-Han route.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Wanyan Kui encamped at Baihuli, sent Army Director Wanyan Andai to take Suizhou, and sent Qingshou with five thousand men to hold Chian and sever the Xiang-Han route.

sentences.zh: 行與宋兵遇，斬首五百級，宋隨州將雷太尉遁去，遂克隨州。

translations.literal: On the march he met Song troops, took five hundred heads, the Song defender of Suizhou Grand Master Lei fled, and Suizhou was captured.
translations.idiomatic: En route he met Song forces, slew five hundred men, drove off Suizhou's defender Grand Master Lei, and captured the city.

sentences.zh: 於是宋鄧城、樊城戍兵皆潰，遂與大軍渡漢江，圍襄陽。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Song garrisons of Dengcheng and Fancheng all collapsed; he then crossed the Han River with the main army and besieged Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Song garrisons at Dengcheng and Fancheng collapsed; he crossed the Han with the main army and besieged Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 元帥匡表薦慶壽謀略出眾。

translations.literal: Commander Kui memorialized recommending Qingshou for outstanding strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Kui memorialized praising Qingshou's exceptional strategy.

sentences.zh: 上嘉之，進一官，遷拱衛直都指揮使，提點如故。

translations.literal: The emperor commended him, promoted him one rank, transferred him to commander of the Palace Guard Direct Corps, and retained him as intendant.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him, promoted him one rank, made him commander of the Palace Guard Direct Corps, and kept him as intendant.

sentences.zh: 貞祐二年，遷元帥右都監，以保全平州功進官五階，賜金吐鶻、重幣十端。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyou he was transferred to right army director of the commander-in-chief; for preserving Pingzhou he was promoted five ranks and granted a golden gyrfalcon and ten lengths of heavy gifts.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenyou he became right army director; for saving Pingzhou he was promoted five ranks and given a golden gyrfalcon and ten lengths of heavy brocade.

sentences.zh: 頃之，宣宗遷汴，改右副點檢兼侍衛親軍副都指揮使。

translations.literal: Before long, when Xuanzong moved to Bian, he was made right deputy inspector and concurrently deputy commander of the Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after Xuanzong moved to Bian, he was made right deputy inspector and deputy commander of the Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 閱月，知大興府事。

translations.literal: After a month he was appointed to administer Daxing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: A month later he was put in charge of Daxing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 未行，改左副點檢兼親軍副都指揮。

translations.literal: Before he took up the post he was changed to left deputy inspector and concurrently deputy commander of the Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the post he was made left deputy inspector and deputy commander of the Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 數月，知彰德府事。

translations.literal: Several months later he was appointed to administer Zhangde Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Months later he governed Zhangde Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 三年，中都危急，改元帥左都監，將大名兵萬八千、西南路步騎萬一千、河北兵一萬救中都。

translations.literal: In the third year, when the Central Capital was in peril, he was made left army director of the commander-in-chief and led eighteen thousand from the Daming army, eleven thousand infantry and cavalry of the Southwest circuit, and ten thousand Hebei troops to relieve the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, as the Central Capital faced ruin, he became left army director and marched eighteen thousand Daming troops, eleven thousand Southwest circuit horse and foot, and ten thousand Hebei soldiers to its relief.

sentences.zh: 次霸州北，兵潰。

translations.literal: He halted north of Bazhou and the army collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Camped north of Bazhou, his army disintegrated.

sentences.zh: 頃之，中都不守，改大名府權宣撫使。

translations.literal: Before long the Central Capital fell; he was made acting pacification commissioner of Daming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after the Central Capital fell, he was made acting pacification commissioner of Daming.

sentences.zh: 未幾，知河中府，權河東南路宣撫副使。

translations.literal: Before long he administered Hezhong Prefecture and acted as deputy pacification commissioner of the Hedong South circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he governed Hezhong Prefecture and served as acting deputy pacification commissioner of the Hedong South circuit.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷元帥左監軍兼陝西統軍使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to left army supervisor of the commander-in-chief and concurrently commander-in-chief of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he became left army supervisor and commander-in-chief of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 駐兵延安，敗夏人于安塞堡。

translations.literal: He stationed troops at Yan'an and defeated the Xia at Ansaibao.
translations.idiomatic: Encamped at Yan'an, he defeated the Western Xia at Ansaibao.

sentences.zh: 戰于鄜州之倉曲谷，有功。

translations.literal: He fought at Cangqu Valley in Fuzhou and won merit.
translations.idiomatic: At Cangqu Valley in Fuzhou he fought with distinction.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：承暉守中都期年，相為存亡，臨終就義，古人所難也。

translations.literal: The eulogy says: Cheng Hui held the Central Capital for a full year, sharing life and death with it, and at the end died for righteousness—a thing hard even for men of old.
translations.idiomatic: The eulogy reads: Cheng Hui held the Central Capital for a year, bound to its fate, and at the end died for the realm—an act even ancients found hard.

sentences.zh: 大抵宣宗既遷，則中都必不能守，中都不守，則土崩之勢決矣。

translations.literal: In general, once Xuanzong had moved away the Central Capital could not be held; once it was not held, the collapse of the realm was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xuanzong had moved south, the Central Capital could not be saved; once it fell, the empire's collapse was sealed.

sentences.zh: 僕散端、耿端義似忠而實愚，抹撚盡忠委中都，庸何議焉。

translations.literal: Pu Sanduan and Geng Duanyi seemed loyal but were in fact foolish; Monian Jinzhong entrusted the Central Capital and fled—what is there to discuss?
translations.idiomatic: Pu Sanduan and Geng Duanyi seemed loyal but were foolish; Monian Jinzhong abandoned the capital—little need be said of them.

sentences.zh: 高琪忌承暉成功，孛朮魯德裕緩師期，奸人之党，於是何誅。

translations.literal: Gao Qi envied Cheng Hui's success, Bei Pailu Deyu was slow in the campaign schedule—the faction of treacherous men: how could they not be punished?
translations.idiomatic: Gao Qi resented Cheng Hui's success, Bei Pailu Deyu missed the march—such a clique of traitors deserved whatever befell them.

sentences.zh: 李英被酒敗軍，雖死不能贖也。

translations.literal: Li Ying, drunk, ruined the army—even death could not atone.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ying, drunk, destroyed his army—even death could not redeem him.

sentences.zh: 烏古論慶壽無罰，貞祐之刑政，從可知矣。

translations.literal: Wugulun Qingshou went unpunished—from this the punishments and government of Zhenyou may be known.
translations.idiomatic: Wugulun Qingshou escaped punishment—enough to show what justice meant under Zhenyou.
